flags.excerpt: Some economists who have modelled agricultural output give weather a real but minority share of the fall.
flags.explanation: The weather is one of the four blame positions the student explicitly asked about, and it is the only subsection of section 7 where no scholar or document is named. The 'official Chinese explanation for decades' is not pinned to the citable 1981 Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party, and the economists who quantified the weather's share are left anonymous. Every other position (Dikotter, Bernstein, MacFarquhar, Yang, Sen, Lin and Yang, Thaxton) gets a name, year and work; the student cannot write 'according to X' for the Party line or for the quantified weather share, which is exactly the gap the teacher's comment identified.
flags.required_fix: Name the CCP's 1981 Resolution as the source of the 'natural disasters plus leftist errors' line, and name at least one quantitative study with its approximate weather share (for example Li Wei and Dennis Tao Yang, Journal of Political Economy 2005, or Kung and Lin, 2003), flagged as recalled, so the weather position meets the same attribution standard as the other three.

summary: All four request items are answered substantively with accurate, checkable specifics. i1: dated timeline (May 1958 adoption, Beidaihe August 1958 with 26,000 communes and the 10.7 million tonne steel target, Lushan 2 July to 16 August 1959 with Peng Dehuai's 14 July letter, his September dismissal and replacement by Lin Biao, Twelve Articles November 1960, Sixty Articles 1961), the SSB grain series (195/200/170/143.5/147.5/160 million tonnes) and crude death rates flagged as later-revised official data, and the causal mechanism (exaggeration to 375 million tonnes, procurement rising from 48 to 67 million tonnes against a falling harvest, 4 million tonnes exported in 1959, mess halls, labour diversion, Lysenkoist close planting and deep ploughing, Four Pests). The 1962 meeting is correctly the Seven Thousand Cadres Conference, 11 January to 7 February 1962, with the three-parts-natural, seven-parts-man-made verdict attributed to Liu Shaoqi. i2: an eleven-row death-toll table with named authors, years, works and method (Jiang Zhenghua 17m, Peng Xizhe 23m, Coale 27m, Ashton et al. 30m, Banister 30m, Becker 30m, Cao Shuji 32.5m, Yang Jisheng 36m, Chang and Halliday 38m, Dikotter 45m, Sun Jingxian a few million), plus O Grada's 2011 critique and a section on why estimates differ (baseline, under-registration, lost births, year range, provincial extrapolation). i3: the blame debate is mapped with attribution for Mao personally, the system, local cadres and weather/Soviets, including provincial leaders Wu Zhipu, Li Jingquan and Zeng Xisheng. i4: the Shanghai March 1959 remark is presented as disputed, Dikotter's 45 million is not treated as accepted, and section 8 separates settled facts, distrusted data, estimates and interpretation. I checked the figures and attributions and found no fabricated numbers, no misattributed books, no misdating of Lushan, and no claim that Mao lost power. One minor gap: the weather subsection is the only blame position without a named citable source (no 1981 Resolution, anonymous 'some economists'). Outside my categories: the Z3 finding INT-SUBJ-001 is a parser artefact, since 'during 1961 and 1962' modifies 'abandoned', not 'launched', and the sentence's chronology is correct; the sources line cites 'course notes' although supplied.json is empty, which is a sourcing matter for the format gate and Overseer B.
